messages:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — we need a lightweight way to choose ordering between the 'Fincorp private integration' ask and the 'dedicated throughput uplift' initiative. Both are customer-facing and we have limited engineering headcount. Thoughts on balancing near-term revenue risk vs longer-term unit cost?
Raj Patel: Short take: map expected net ARR impact over the next 12 months versus engineering weeks required. Penalize cross-team blockers (x1.5). Keeps decisions data-driven and pragmatic.
Lina Gomez: +1. Run a compact RICE-style table but keep it simple: Reach = # accounts affected (est), Impact = % retention/lift, Confidence = 0.1–1, Effort = eng-weeks. Use same time horizon for Reach.
Tom Rivers: From infra POV, throughput uplift is ~6w (2 infra changes + storage migration). Private integration MVP is ~4w but triggers security review & legal signoff which historically adds queue time.
Samir Kaur: UX gating: Fincorp needs an approval flow mock + audit UX — add ~1w for verification loops. Also if we delay throughput work, some demo customers will hit rate limits and that will break sales cycles.
Raj Patel: Example quick calc (illustrative):
Fincorp MVP: Reach=5 accounts (hot), Impact=0.25 retention, Confidence=0.6, Effort=4 -> score=(Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort = 0.1875
Throughput uplift: Reach=50k tokens/day (broad), Impact=0.1, Confidence=0.7, Effort=6 -> normalize Reach to same scale -> score ~0.58. So infra looks higher if you only use token reach.
Maya Chen: Helpful — but sales says two deals (~$120k ARR) will slip without the private path. How do we fold deal-level urgency into the model?
Tom Rivers: Add a "deal ARR at risk" column and convert it into an urgency multiplier. If deal ARR > threshold, multiply total score by 1.4. Also list blocking tickets so we can see lead time.
Lina Gomez: Alternative: split work. Deliver a narrow private MVP (just auth + audit log export + minimal contract) in ~2w to unblock deals, then schedule the throughput sprint next quarter. That reduces cross-team friction.
Samir Kaur: Agree on the split. Proposed launch gating for the private MVP: (1) legal signoff OK, (2) audit logging turned on, (3) customer acceptance test passing. If all three, sales can close.
Maya Chen: Action items: 1) Raj — draft the numeric table with real inputs & include a "deal ARR at risk" column (EOD). 2) Tom — enumerate infra blocking tickets + estimated queue wait (by EOD). 3) Lina & Samir — sketch a 2w MVP scope + acceptance criteria (tomorrow morning). We'll reconvene 11:00 UTC tomorrow to pick ordering.
DevBot: Calendar invite created: "product: initiative orchestration" — 2024-05-13 11:00 UTC.
Raj Patel: I'll add a simple sensitivity column (how much the score flips if Confidence moves ±20%). Good to see where assumptions bite.
Maya Chen: Perfect. If anyone spots a hidden dependency (billing, SSO, or compliance) ping here immediately. :thumbsup:
